```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import math
import re

import torch
from torch import nn

text = open("data/shakespeare.txt").read()
chars = sorted(set(text))
n_chars = len(chars)
index = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(chars)}
ids = torch.tensor([index[ch] for ch in text])
n_train = 90_000
train_ids, val_ids = ids[:n_train], ids[n_train:]


def decode(t):
    return "".join(chars[i] for i in t.tolist())


print(n_chars, len(text))
print(text[:120])
```

The exercises use a local copy, [`data/shakespeare.txt`](data/shakespeare.txt),
of the first `r format(nchar(py$text), big.mark = ",")` characters of the [tiny Shakespeare text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt).
@karpathy2015charrnn collected that text from Shakespeare's plays.
`tools/get-shakespeare.py` rebuilds the copy.
The script keeps only the first `r format(nchar(py$text), big.mark = ",")` characters,
the opening of *Coriolanus*,
and changes nothing else.
The copy has `r py$n_chars` distinct characters,
counting capitals, punctuation, the space and the line break separately.
`ids` numbers each character by its place in the sorted list `chars`.
The first `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` characters are for training,
and the remaining `r format(nchar(py$text) - py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` for validation.
